title: I Let the Hackerspace Resin-Printer Queue Catch the Founder

parts.text: I queued a four-hour print at 10:02 p.m. and the founder started a twelve-hour chess set on my vat. The queue board he built said: FIFO. FOUNDERS BOOK LIKE MEMBERS. I was twenty-eight, night member, holding a confirmed slot. Founder Max said, "Calibrations don't queue." The slicer file was a chess set. I photographed the board, the file name, and my confirmation. Then I let the queue bot cancel any job not matching the slot owner. At 10:08 the bot posted why Max's name was on a queue-jump ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The bot can see a chess set on a vat locked to my four-hour slot.

social.video_title: The founder called a chess set a calibration — Part 1/2
social.description: Night vat, a twelve-hour jump, and a FIFO board he built. The bot cancelled him. Would you have waited until morning?

parts.text: Max called it a joke until Slack filled with the bot. I printed the ticket, the board, and the photo. My print started. Max booked noon like a member and told the space the board was always about optics. Optics is a word founders use when a bot exists. Printer policy now has a second line: CHESS IS NOT CALIBRATION. I pull a clean plate. Max FIFOs. The vat finally smells like my resin.

social.video_title: Chess is not a calibration — Part 2/2
social.description: Queue-jump ticket, a real four-hour print, and a second line on the board. Was founding ever a chess set?
